name: Atlas
summary: Atlas is a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer pretrained from scratch on text, images, video, camera poses and 3D data. Its organising idea is that standard multimodal models flatten everything into one- or two-dimensional sequences, which makes spatial tasks unnecessarily hard; Atlas instead encodes inputs into a shared spatial context where each image is grounded at a 3D position, and treats camera geometry as a native input rather than something coaxed out of a text prompt. The same model generates camera-controlled video up to a minute at 1440p, reconstructs scenes from as few as two or three photos into point clouds and Gaussian splats, and simulates space and time together for robot Real-to-Sim workflows over rigid, articulated and deformable objects. World Labs reports 93% human preference over FLUX 3 on camera-controlled generation and 25.3 AbsRel on 3D reconstruction against 28.7 for the next-best baseline, and says each increase in pretraining compute unlocked new capabilities.
innovation: 3D-grounded spatial context: inputs are anchored at positions in space rather than flattened into token sequences.
Camera pose as a native modality, giving geometric rather than linguistic control over viewpoint.
Generation, reconstruction and simulation unified in one pretrained model instead of three specialised ones.
matters: The strongest argument yet that the world model a robot needs is 3D and camera-native rather than a video generator — the opposite bet from the video-diffusion world-action models.
It is the engine behind World Labs' real-to-sim pipeline, which is where the robotics payoff actually lands.
limits: Early access with select partners; no weights, no code, no paper, and no independent evaluation.
Reported comparisons are against generative video and reconstruction baselines, not against robot-policy outcomes — its manipulation value is so far argued rather than measured.
Human-preference win rates are World Labs' own evaluations.
lineage: Marble's 3D scene generation rebuilt as a from-scratch multimodal foundation model with camera geometry as a first-class input.
